**STEP 1 - Vessel:** Flat round plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, and the food sits flat on it.

**STEP 2 - Scale:** The plate spans about 480 px. The apple is about 130 px across, and a whole apple is about 7.5 cm, so 17.5 px/cm. Plate width = 480 / 17.5 ≈ 27 cm. This falls in the round dinner plate range (25-28 cm), so I use 27 cm.

**STEP 3 - Items:**
- **Cherry tomatoes:** I count 10 visible. Allowing about 1 hidden, that is 11 × 15 g ≈ 165 g.
- **Apple:** One whole apple, about 180 g.
- **Yellow halved fruit/pepper piece:** Roughly 60 g.
- **Cauliflower:** Patch about 230 × 200 px gives 230 × 200 × 0.8 / 17.5² ≈ 96 cm². Average thickness about 2 cm, so volume ≈ 190 ml. At 0.6 g/ml, ≈ 115 g.
- **Carrot slices:** Footprint about 70 cm² (the patch is partly gapped), thickness about 1.5 cm, so volume ≈ 105 ml. At 0.6 g/ml, ≈ 65-80 g. I use 80 g.

**STEP 4 - Hidden food:** No base layer is visible under the food on the plate, so none is added.

**STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:** Cherry tomato 18, apple 52, yellow pepper 31, cauliflower 25, carrot 35.

Total ≈ 600 g, roughly 2.7 kcal per gram on average. Estimated energy ≈ 165×0.18 + 180×0.52 + 60×0.31 + 115×0.25 + 80×0.35 ≈ 30 + 94 + 19 + 29 + 28 ≈ 200 kcal.
